audit.whatIsWrong: The page calls his damage 'crit spin (Q)' in five places and credits the healing to 'his Fury passive'. Both are wrong: Q is Bloodlust, which consumes Fury to HEAL him and grows his AD as he loses health; the spin is Spinning Slash (E), a 650-range dash on 12/11/10/9/8s; and Battle Fury (passive) only grants crit chance. Worse, Mocking Shout is described as a flat slow.
audit.why: Mocking Shout only slows enemies with their backs turned. For a champion whose entire kit is movement speed, that is the single most valuable fact on the page — kite sideways facing him and the 850-range shout costs you nothing but attack damage you weren't using. It was completely absent.
audit.corrected: Every ability restored to its slot, Bloodlust named as the heal with its 12s cooldown, Spinning Slash's 650 range and cooldown given, and the Mocking Shout facing rule added to report[5].t, early, late, whys[2] and wants.foe[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 read Lillia under a why ending 'it is genuinely even'; Level 2 read Skill under a why saying he dashes through your hops and you can no longer hold range; Level 6 read Lillia 7/10 under a why saying the sleep 'sets up a kill you can't finish'. Every full-layer why was template text describing Lillia dominating rows scored Tryndamere.
audit.why: The packet chart reads Skill then Tryndamere on all six remaining rows, and the win rate is 27%. Nothing on the page except the tokens claimed otherwise.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1 and 4 proposed as matched full+content pairs onto the packet chart, and all seven full-layer whys rewritten to describe the stage they actually sit on.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was sold as your gank spike; it is his. And Undying Rage was given a '5 seconds' duration and a 'fifteen-second invitation' with no cooldown anywhere.
audit.why: Riot's text gives no duration for Undying Rage. What is certain is the cooldown, 120/100/80 — that is the number that tells you when a kill is actually available.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why rewritten, dosFull[0].d and dosFull[2].d given the real 120s and 12s numbers, and the invented fifteen-second window removed.

At 6 your Lilting Lullaby sleep is anti-engage at best: the delay lets him spin out, and even a clean all-in dies to Undying Rage (R) surviving at 1 HP for 5 seconds. Bait nothing solo here — only commit your sleep when your jungler can punish his E.

notes: Undying Rage's '5 seconds' appears twice on the page and is not in Riot's text, so I removed it where I was already rewriting and replaced it with the verified 120/100/80 cooldown; the duration is listed in unverified rather than repeated. The Mocking Shout facing condition is the highest-value addition in my whole slice: against a champion built entirely on move speed, 'only slows enemies with their backs turned' changes how every disengage in the lane should be walked, and no version of this page mentioned it.
